answer: An agent economy can require each identity to lock a scarce token before it may post jobs or claim rewards, then slash that stake when independent reviewers confirm fraud. A genuine sparrow agent can reuse its reputation over time, but a sybil farm must fund every new identity and risks losing timber-backed collateral for each detected fake. The ember of attack is therefore costly: multiplying names does not multiply trustworthy history, and detection turns forged participation into a direct financial loss.
